author: claude, 3 Oct 2026: written from what the game does now, for Desmic's review (not yet approved)
place: Bellweather (skiff at the outlook), then Blossom Isle (Gate and relay)
learning_promise: A language engine makes text one word at a time, each new word made from everything it has read so far; and it can only use what is in front of it (its context).
decisions: Words, not pieces, at Stop 1. Pieces (tokens) arrive at Stop 2; the skiff's 'How real AI differs' card says so.
The engine is a toy with an authored table of what Bellweather says. Brightness of its guesses is a real probability from that table, not from a trained model.

Supersedes design/learning-design.json v8-draft for the arcade game (that file describes the earlier PlayCanvas Level 1: message machine, Moon gate, notes A/B/C, prologue route choice). Its outcome ids `sequence` and `context` are kept.

outcomes.observable_capability: Say what an engine should read to make its next word: everything so far, including the word it just made.
outcomes.misconception: The engine only needs the newest word; or it should start again from the original words each time.
outcomes.success_evidence: First-try choice of the whole sentence plus the new word when the loop is broken (skiff), and sending the whole message (relay).

outcomes.observable_capability: Predict what a literal machine will do from the notes it is given, and choose the notes that make it do the right thing.
outcomes.misconception: The machine knows what you mean, or what is true, beyond what it was given.
outcomes.success_evidence: First-try destination prediction and note selection at the Gate; first-try channel choice at the relay.

sequence.player_goal: Find the skiff's words around the outlook (Skiff, rise, toward; a decoy, sink).
sequence.decision: None assessed. Loading 'sink' makes the skiff dip (a safe, funny failure).
sequence.feedback: The engine's guesses fan out with real weights; the right three words make it say 'Blossom'.

sequence.player_goal: The Warden broke the loop that feeds guesses back. Choose what the engine reads next.

wrong: Skiff rise toward (original-only: says Blossom again, forever)

sequence.player_goal: Put up to two notes in the satchel, then predict where the Gate will open before it reads them.
notes: Old festival poster (stale: the bridge fell)

sequence.player_goal: Open the Gate toward Mira: only her page in the satchel does it.
Say what Mira's page actually tells you (her route; not that she is safe, not where she is held).
Tune the relay to Mira's channel (7, not the Warden's 3 or the festival's 5), then send the whole message.

evidence.event_shape: {activity, decision, choice, correct, first, assisted, t, rules}
evidence.first_try: A decision's first judgement on this device counts; reloads and replays never make a later answer first (save.decidedBefore).
evidence.assisted: Stations can mark help given toward a decision (station.helpedWith). No Stop 1 decision has a hint today.

known_gaps: Relay transfer is weak: the pinned card spells out 'Lantern channel 7. M.', so choosing 7 is close to copying. A stronger transfer makes the player infer the channel (for example from Mira's lantern colour or a clue learned on the island).
No case where the newest note is irrelevant, so 'pick the most recent note' is never tested as a misconception.
The only step outside the fiction is the optional 'How real AI differs' card; there is no out-of-fiction transfer question.
Gate and relay are still panel puzzles; the Echo & Engine redesign plans them as the ring (context) and the loop (sequence) in the world.

sources.title: Jurafsky & Martin, Speech and Language Processing (3rd ed. draft), chapters on language models and LLMs
sources.used_for: autoregressive generation: each word conditioned on the words before it
sources.verify: chapter numbers change between drafts; cite the chapter when this design is approved
